questions.text: In an undirected connected planar graph G, there are eight vertices and five faces. The number of edges in G is _________.
questions.solution:
Euler's formula for a connected planar graph: V [latex]-[/latex] E + F = 2.

8 [latex]-[/latex] E + 5 = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] E = 11

Answer: 11

questions.text:
Let p and q be two propositions. Consider the following two formulae in propositional logic.

[latex]S1: (\neg p\wedge(p\vee q))\rightarrow q[/latex]
[latex]S2: q\rightarrow(\neg p\wedge(p\vee q))[/latex]

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: [latex] eg p\wedge(p\vee q)\equiv eg p\wedge q[/latex], and [latex]( eg p\wedge q) ightarrow q[/latex] is always true [latex] ightarrow[/latex] tautology.
- S2: take p = q = 1: q is true but [latex] eg p\wedge(p\vee q)[/latex] is false [latex] ightarrow[/latex] S2 is false [latex] ightarrow[/latex] not a tautology.

Answer: S1 is a tautology but S2 is not a tautology

options: Both S1 and S2 are tautologies.
S1 is a tautology but S2 is not a tautology
S1 is not a tautology but S2 is a tautology

questions.text: If [latex]A=\{x, y, z\}[/latex] and [latex]B=\{u, v, w, x\}[/latex], and the universe is [latex]\{s, t, u, v, w, x, y, z\}[/latex]. Then [latex](A \cup \bar{B}) \cap(A \cap B)[/latex] is equal to
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]\bar B=\{s,t,y,z\}[/latex], so [latex]A\cup\bar B=\{s,t,x,y,z\}[/latex]
- [latex]A\cap B=\{x\}[/latex]

[latex]\{s,t,x,y,z\}\cap\{x\}=\{x\}[/latex]

(This question was excluded from ISRO's evaluation.)

Answer: {x}

questions.text:
Given that
B(a) means "a is a bear"
F(a) means "a is a fish" and
E(a,b) means "a eats b"
Then what is the best meaning of
[latex]\forall x[F(x) \rightarrow \forall y(E(y, x) \rightarrow b(y))][/latex]
questions.solution:
Read it as: for every x that is a fish, every y that eats x is a bear. In other words, anything that eats a fish is a bear: only bears eat fish. It does not say that bears eat fish or that every fish gets eaten.

Answer: Only bears eat fish

options: Every fish is eaten by some bear

Which of the following is correct for the above distributions?
questions.solution:
Distribution B (frequencies 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is the mirror image of A (5, 4, 3, 2, 1). Mirroring changes the mean but not the spread, so the standard deviations are equal.

Answer: Standard deviation of A is same as standard deviation of B
